parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/Server.ts does what an infrastructure composition root does. It sets up the Express app and JSON body parsing, creates the in-memory repositories, wires them into the application use cases and controllers, maps HTTP routes to controller handlers, adds an error handler that maps errors to HTTP 500, and starts the HTTP listener. All of these are framework, transport or wiring concerns that belong in infrastructure. The `initializeData` seeding only puts fixture Product entities into the in-memory store at startup. It is bootstrap data, not a business rule: there is no validation, no state transition and no stock logic. The file contains no domain or application rules, such as order state checks or stock checks. A side note that is outside this rule: the error handler takes only three parameters, so Express will not treat it as error middleware. That is a correctness bug, not a layer-responsibility problem.
